name: Grade 7 IIIT: micro:bit Sensor Systems
description: micro:bit input-output systems, ultrasonic distance readings, thresholds, Bluetooth signals, sound outputs, test tables, reliability, and the Mandrake project.

words.definition: A small programmable computer used with sensors and outputs.
A part that detects information from the environment.
Using high-frequency sound to measure distance.
words.example: The ultrasonic sensor detected whether the object was close.

words.definition: How far apart two things are.
words.example: Distance changed when the Mandrake was removed.

words.definition: A limit value used to decide when output should happen.
words.example: The threshold triggered the scream sound.

words.definition: A wireless method for sending data over short distances.
words.example: Bluetooth sent the signal to the computer.

words.definition: Information sent from one part of a system to another.
words.example: The microbit sent a signal when the distance changed.

words.definition: To cause an action to happen.
words.example: The threshold triggered the output sound.

words.definition: The logic or decision step in a system.
words.example: The process compared distance with the threshold.

words.definition: The action or result produced by a system.
words.example: The output was a scream sound.

words.definition: A labeled drawing that shows system parts and connections.
words.example: The diagram labeled input, process, output, and signal.

words.definition: A table used to record test conditions and results.
words.example: The test table stored five distance readings.

words.definition: What you think should happen before testing.
words.example: The expected result was sound when distance was high.

words.definition: What really happened during a test.
words.example: The actual result showed the threshold was too low.

words.definition: How dependably a system works in repeated tests.
words.example: Reliability improved after changing the sensor angle.

words.definition: A model or imitation used when real equipment is unavailable.
words.example: The group presented a labeled simulation.

words.definition: A record of project plans, tests, issues, and improvements.
words.example: The logbook showed the best threshold.
